# Appendix: Tool catalog

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-tool-catalog.mjs from a running build. Do not edit by hand: change the descriptions in that script and run it again. -->

Tools are the actions Sachivji can take. Each specialist holds only some of them (see [Agents and roles](05-agents-and-roles.md)). In **Auto** mode the main assistant can use the tools of every specialist directly as well. A tool that "changes things" always asks for your approval first, unless you switched on auto-approve for it.

The same list, with full descriptions, is in **Settings > Tools by role**.

## Planner

Turns a complex or ambiguous request into ordered steps. Has no tools and executes nothing — hands each step to Researcher, Developer, Data Access or the other specialists.

No tools of its own: it only reasons and plans.

## Researcher

Researches the web deeply: reads many pages, keeps notes, finds stock photos, saves findings to a file. Does not recall past chats (History Analyst) or call configured APIs (Data Access).

| Tool | What it does | Changes things? |
|---|---|---|
| `web_search` | Searches the web (Tavily when a key is set, otherwise DuckDuckGo) and returns ranked results. | No |
| `parse_html` | Reads a web page (URL, file or pasted HTML) and returns the clean article text without menus and ads. | No |
| `download_image` | Downloads images from web addresses into the workspace `resources` folder (up to 5 MB each). | Yes, asks first |
| `find_stock_images` | Finds free stock photos on a topic, with creator and licence, ready to download. | No |
| `save_research_note` | Saves a finding with its source while researching. | No |
| `read_research_notes` | Reads back all saved research notes in order. | No |
| `write_file` | Creates or overwrites a text file in the workspace. | Yes, asks first |
| `get_environment` | Tells the assistant about your setup: workspace folders, operating system, today's date, Python status. | No |

## History Analyst

Recalls and compares things from earlier conversations, including how a detail changed over time. Does not search the web (Researcher).

| Tool | What it does | Changes things? |
|---|---|---|
| `search_history` | Searches your past conversations (including this one) by meaning and returns excerpts with session and date. | No |
| `get_environment` | Tells the assistant about your setup: workspace folders, operating system, today's date, Python status. | No |

## Developer

Writes AND runs code (Python in the workspace venv), edits files, uses git, cloud CLIs and GitHub. Not for plain Word documents (Text Document Creator) or database queries (Data Access).

| Tool | What it does | Changes things? |
|---|---|---|
| `read_file` | Reads a text file. | No |
| `list_directory` | Lists the files and folders in a directory. | No |
| `find_files` | Finds files by name pattern under a folder. | No |
| `find_in_files` | Searches the text inside files (like grep) under a folder. | No |
| `write_file` | Creates or overwrites a text file in the workspace. | Yes, asks first |
| `shell_execute` | Runs a shell command in the workspace. | Yes, asks first |
| `python_run` | Runs Python code in the workspace's own Python environment (charts, data, Word and Excel files). | Yes, asks first |
| `git_exec` | Runs git commands on the workspace repository (read-only commands need no confirmation). | Sometimes, asks first |
| `git_clone_repo` | Clones a different git repository into its own fresh folder, to inspect it. | Yes, asks first |
| `aws_cli` | Runs the AWS command line tool, if installed and signed in. | Yes, asks first |
| `azure_cli` | Runs the Azure command line tool, if installed and signed in. | Yes, asks first |
| `gcloud_cli` | Runs the Google Cloud command line tool, if installed and signed in. | Yes, asks first |
| `github_cli` | Runs the GitHub command line tool (`gh`) for issues, pull requests and releases. | Yes, asks first |
| `show_media` | Shows an image from the workspace in the chat. | No |
| `get_environment` | Tells the assistant about your setup: workspace folders, operating system, today's date, Python status. | No |

## Data Access

Queries configured databases and calls configured external APIs. Not for local files (Data Processor) or for creating connections (Configurator).

| Tool | What it does | Changes things? |
|---|---|---|
| `db_list_connections` | Lists the database connections you configured (never their passwords). | No |
| `db_introspect_schema` | Lists the tables and columns of a database connection. | No |
| `db_execute_sql` | Runs SQL on a database connection (anything that changes data asks first). | Sometimes, asks first |
| `db_list_rows` | Lists rows of a table, a page at a time, with no SQL needed. | No |
| `db_count_rows` | Counts the rows of a table. | No |
| `db_find_rows` | Finds rows where one column equals a value. | No |
| `db_save_query` | Saves a working query with parameters as a reusable tool for next time. | Yes, asks first |
| `api_list_connections` | Lists the external API connections you configured. | No |
| `api_introspect` | Discovers an API's endpoints from its OpenAPI/Swagger description. | No |
| `api_call` | Makes an authenticated call to a configured API (calls that change things ask first). | Sometimes, asks first |
| `api_check_status` | Checks on a long-running API job started earlier. | No |
| `get_environment` | Tells the assistant about your setup: workspace folders, operating system, today's date, Python status. | No |

## Data Processor

Reads, queries and transforms local CSV, JSON, XML and Excel files. Not for databases (Data Access) or general programming (Developer).

| Tool | What it does | Changes things? |
|---|---|---|
| `parse_csv` | Summarises and queries a CSV file, and can append a record, without reading the whole file into the chat. | Sometimes, asks first |
| `parse_json` | Summarises and queries a JSON document, and can append a record. | Sometimes, asks first |
| `parse_xml` | Summarises and queries an XML document. | No |
| `xlsx_read` | Reads an Excel workbook. | No |
| `xlsx_write` | Creates or changes an Excel workbook. | Yes, asks first |
| `read_file` | Reads a text file. | No |
| `list_directory` | Lists the files and folders in a directory. | No |
| `find_files` | Finds files by name pattern under a folder. | No |
| `get_environment` | Tells the assistant about your setup: workspace folders, operating system, today's date, Python status. | No |

## Text Document Creator

Creates, fills from templates and reads Word and other Office documents. Cannot run code or draw charts from data (Developer) and cannot edit an existing file in place.

| Tool | What it does | Changes things? |
|---|---|---|
| `office_read_document` | Reads the text of a Word or PowerPoint file. | No |
| `office_create_document` | Creates a new Word or PowerPoint file from scratch. | Yes, asks first |
| `office_fill_template` | Fills one of your Word/PowerPoint templates, keeping its styling. | Sometimes, asks first |
| `office_extract_template` | Turns an existing document into a reusable template. | Sometimes, asks first |
| `read_file` | Reads a text file. | No |
| `list_directory` | Lists the files and folders in a directory. | No |
| `find_files` | Finds files by name pattern under a folder. | No |
| `get_environment` | Tells the assistant about your setup: workspace folders, operating system, today's date, Python status. | No |

## Configurator

Sets up connections to databases, external APIs and MCP servers. Does not query them (Data Access); secrets go through the confirmation dialog, never chat.

| Tool | What it does | Changes things? |
|---|---|---|
| `db_create_connection` | Sets up a database connection from details you give in chat (the password goes in the confirmation dialog). | Yes, asks first |
| `api_create_connection` | Sets up an external API connection from details you give in chat. | Yes, asks first |
| `mcp_create_connection` | Sets up an MCP server connection from details you give in chat. | Yes, asks first |
| `mcp_list_connections` | Lists your MCP servers, whether each is connected, and the tools each offers. | No |
| `get_environment` | Tells the assistant about your setup: workspace folders, operating system, today's date, Python status. | No |

## MCP Operator

Uses the tools of connected MCP servers (wikis, knowledge bases, integrations). Not for the open web (Researcher), databases (Data Access) or past chats (History Analyst).

| Tool | What it does | Changes things? |
|---|---|---|
| `mcp_list_connections` | Lists your MCP servers, whether each is connected, and the tools each offers. | No |
| `get_environment` | Tells the assistant about your setup: workspace folders, operating system, today's date, Python status. | No |

## Page Creator

Designs one slide of a presentation from a brief. Not conversational and never a plan step — the top-level assistant calls it once per slide.

| Tool | What it does | Changes things? |
|---|---|---|
| `pptx_compose_slide` | Lays out one slide (text, images, shapes, charts, tables) from a brief. | No |

## Email

Drafts and sends an email from a brief (recipients, what to say). Does not write documents (Text Document Creator) or look up addresses (Data Access).

| Tool | What it does | Changes things? |
|---|---|---|
| `list_email_connections` | Lists your email accounts (never their secrets). | No |
| `send_email` | Sends an email from a configured account (always asks first). | Yes, asks first |
| `get_environment` | Tells the assistant about your setup: workspace folders, operating system, today's date, Python status. | No |

## Tools that belong to the main assistant

These are not held by a specialist: the main assistant uses them directly.

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `describe_capabilities` | Tells you what the assistant can do, which specialists exist and which connections are configured. |
| `pptx_start_deck`, `pptx_add_slide`, `pptx_save_deck` | Build a PowerPoint presentation one slide at a time, using the Page Creator for each slide. |
| `delegate_to_<specialist>` | Hands a job to a specialist (one per role). |
| Tools of your MCP servers and saved queries | Appear while the matching connection exists. MCP tools belong to the MCP Operator. |
